newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan reforms would make it major market -- Fed.
newsitem.headline: Japan reforms would make it major market -- Fed.

text.p: An official of Japan's Finance Ministry quoted William McDonough, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, as saying on Tuesday that Japan would be a central financial market in Asia if it carried out financial reforms.
McDonough made the remarks during a meeting with Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, the official said.
McDonough and Mitsuzuka did not talk about exchange rates at all, the ministry official said.
McDonough had said he hoped Japan would carry out "Big Bang" financial reforms. Japan was such an economic power that it would become a central market in Asia, he added.
The official said McDonough had said that the U.S. economy was in an ideal situation, without inflation and with unemployment at a low rate.
McDonough is scheduled to meet Eisuke Sakakibara, director of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, later on Tuesday and to visit the Bank of Japan.
